sugestoes.texto: WHAT: readLength validates content length against the total input length (`limit`) instead of the number of bytes remaining, and skips bounds checking entirely for short-form lengths. WHY: This accepts malformed lengths that exceed the current structure and can reject valid nested lengths, producing incorrect parsing or misleading error messages. HOW: Compute the remaining bytes (`limit - count`) and enforce `length <= remaining` uniformly for both short-form and long-form length encodings.

issues.descricao: Claims getBouncyCastleProvider returns the JDK keystore provider instead of BouncyCastle; that is the intended fallback for the BC-free authz client.
Claims readLength's -1 for indefinite-length encoding breaks length arithmetic or array allocation; the decoder only parses locally generated DER and the sequence path already rejects it.
Claims the lenient sequence parser allows malformed or trailing DER and signature malleability in verification; the parser never sees external signatures.
Claims integerToBytes can silently truncate oversized INTEGER values; inputs come from local signing and always fit the component width.
Claims createECParams/getKeyFactory throwing UnsupportedOperationException breaks EC JWK parsing in the authz client; the client does not use that path.

ASN1Decoder.readInteger passes the -1 returned by readLength for indefinite-length encoding to read(int), which allocates new byte[-1] and throws an unchecked NegativeArraySizeException instead of an IOException on malformed DER input.
integerToBytes silently truncates r/s values longer than the curve size, so non-canonical DER signatures are accepted as different values (signature malleability).
AuthzClient.create eagerly initializes CryptoIntegration, so a shaded/repackaged client that lost its ServiceLoader file fails at construction instead of only when ECDSA is used.

Calling CryptoIntegration.init from AuthzClient.create is claimed to lock the global crypto provider to the minimal AuthzClientCryptoProvider so a later server init is ignored and unsupported operations fail.
The ignored-providers message is passed to logger.debugf as a format string instead of using logger.debug, and keeps a trailing comma.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: record.save return value is ignored in should_block?. WHY: If the update fails (record deleted between read and write, constraint violation, DB error), the match_count/last_match_at stats are silently lost and the method still returns the block decision. HOW: Use record.save! to surface persistence failures, or check save result and handle failure explicitly.

issues.descricao: Claims the rejected-email memory stores the server-normalised email, so it never matches the raw input on retry.
Claims the 'rejectedEmails.@each' dependent key does not observe pushes of plain strings, so the rejection is not shown until the email changes.
BlockedEmail.should_block? returns nil instead of false when the email has no record.
Claims EmailValidator dropped the email format check that the old User#email_validator performed, allowing invalid emails.
Claims EmailValidator#email_in_restriction_setting? raises NoMethodError when the email is nil.
Claims the blocked-email validator specs would still pass if the blocked-email branch were removed.

`rejectedEmails` is declared as an array literal on the controller prototype, so it is shared across instances and modal sessions; emails rejected once keep failing validation later. Initialize it per instance in `init`.

sugestoes.texto: canMapRoles no longer honors user-level manage permission. WHAT: The early return changed from if (canManage(user)) to if (root.hasOneAdminRole(MANAGE_USERS)), dropping the V2 authz manage check for the specific user and the group-chain fallback path for role mapping. WHY: A fine-grained admin with manage permission on a specific user (but without the global MANAGE_USERS role) loses the ability to map roles to that user, breaking the V2 permission model. HOW: Restore the canManage(user) short-circuit or add the equivalent hasPermission(user, MANAGE) / canManageByGroup(user) check.

canManageGroupMembership no longer honors user-level manage permission. WHAT: The early return changed from if (canManage(user)) to if (root.hasOneAdminRole(MANAGE_USERS)). WHY: A fine-grained admin with manage permission on a specific user (but no global MANAGE_USERS role) can no longer manage that user's group membership under V2. HOW: Restore canManage(user) as the short-circuit or add the equivalent user-level manage/group-chain check.

searchForUser no longer filters results through usersEvaluator.canView. WHAT: The .filter(usersEvaluator::canView) call and the guard that limited group-ids to non-global viewers were removed. WHY: If toRepresentation does not re-apply per-user authorization, callers with only group-scoped view permission may receive users they are not authorized to see. HOW: Verify toRepresentation applies canView per user, or restore the filter in searchForUser.

searchForUser no longer filters results through usersEvaluator.canView. WHAT: The filter and the canView guard around group-ids were removed. WHY: If toRepresentation does not re-apply per-user authorization, brute-force user search results may include users the caller is not authorized to view. HOW: Verify downstream filtering in toRepresentation or restore the usersEvaluator::canView filter.

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission iterates all group resources and evaluates permissions per resource. WHAT: findByType over type 'Group' with a hasPermission callback for each group. WHY: Listing/searching users when only group-scoped view is present triggers an authz evaluation per group, causing O(N) growth. HOW: Consider evaluating the all-groups type resource once or batching the evaluation.

issues.descricao: Claims removing the canView filter from searchForUser lets admins see users they are not allowed to view.
getGroupIdsWithViewPermission scans group resources and evaluates permissions for each on every user search or count request.
Claims deleting a group under V2 triggers the removal listener, which calls GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled and throws UnsupportedOperationException.
Claims testManageGroupMembership never exercises the group-level manage-membership permission.
searchForUser no longer filters results with usersEvaluator::canView, so an admin with query access but no view permission and no group grants gets an unrestricted user list.

GroupPermissionsV2.canView(group) does not fall back to canView(), and the PR dropped the canViewGlobal short-circuit, so an admin with an all-groups VIEW permission is denied (and the group filtered out of listings) for any group that has its own permission resource lacking VIEW.
Claims GroupResource management-permissions endpoints call GroupPermissionsV2 methods that throw UnsupportedOperationException, causing 500s when V2 is active.

GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission does not restrict evaluated permissions to the evaluated resource, so when falling back to the all-groups resource a permission granted on one specific group can satisfy the check for any group.

GroupsResource.getGroups no longer hoists the global canView() check, so in FGAP V2 each listed group triggers its own resource lookup and policy evaluation even when an all-groups grant would cover them all.
UserPermissionsV2 canView/canManage dropped AdminRoles.ADMIN from the role check, claimed to deny admins view/manage access unlike V1.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The recreate-upgrade exit code was changed from 4 to 3, and the new feature-disabled condition now uses 4. WHY: This reassigns a previously documented exit-code contract, so existing scripts and automation that treated exit code 4 as 'recreate upgrade required' will now misinterpret recreate-upgrade results as 'feature disabled'. HOW: Keep RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE at 4 and assign FEATURE_DISABLED a different unused value (e.g., 5), or document the breaking change explicitly if backward compatibility is intentionally abandoned.

issues.descricao: Claims the rolling-updates feature is not enabled for the null update strategy in UpgradeTest, so that case tests the operator without the gated feature.
Claims RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 and 4 now means feature disabled, a breaking change that needs release notes.
Claims calling picocli.exit() for the disabled-feature exit code is incorrect because it calls System.exit directly.
Claims `Profile.isFeatureEnabled` in UpdateCompatibilityCheck can hit a null profile and throw NullPointerException because initProfile is skipped for update-compatibility.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The new SQL-expression gate is only applied inside `ReadQuery` and not in the legacy `buildCMDNode` path at nodes.go:160. WHY: When `FlagExpressionParser` is disabled, `buildCMDNode` calls `UnmarshalSQLCommand` directly, bypassing `enableSqlExpressions`; although the stub DB currently makes this fail with a different error, the disable is inconsistent and could be circumvented if the stub is replaced or the error is mishandled. HOW: Move the enablement check into `NewSQLCommand` or `UnmarshalSQLCommand` so all construction paths enforce the same gate.

issues.descricao: enableSqlExpressions always returns false regardless of the sqlExpressions feature flag, so SQL expressions are rejected unconditionally.
The go-duck DB was replaced by a stub whose methods always return 'not implemented', so table parsing and SQL expression execution always fail.
Claims the rejection message says 'not implemented' though the guard is a feature-flag check.
Garbled request to update db.go to use sql.NewInMemoryDB().
Vague claim that the query interface changed and lines 96 and 100 need updating.
enableSqlExpressions returns false on every path (the flag is negated and both branches return false), so SQL expressions are rejected even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled.
Claims TablesList now calls a stub that always errors, so existing parser tests in pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go would break.
The TypeSQL branch in nodes.go reaches UnmarshalSQLCommand → NewSQLCommand → DuckDB parsing without the enableSqlExpressions check, leaving the SQL expression RCE/LFI path reachable.
Existing SQL tests in sql_command_test.go calling NewSQLCommand would now fail because the stubbed DB's TablesList returns 'not implemented', and they were not updated.
Claims that with the stub DB every SQL expression fails parsing and the raw user SQL is logged verbatim, leaking sensitive data.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: permissionCacheUsage is incremented with cache_hit="false" both when the permission cache is actually absent and when the cache is present but checkPermission returns denied. WHY: This makes the metric unable to distinguish a real cache miss from a cached-but-denied permission, changing the semantic meaning of the cache_hit label. HOW: Only increment permissionCacheUsage with cache_hit="false" when getCachedIdentityPermissions returns an error (cache miss); do not increment it when cached permissions exist and simply deny the request.

Stale denial cache can deny access after permissions are granted. Check() consults permDenialCache before permCache and sets it on every DB denial, but never invalidates it when permissions change or when permCache is refreshed. Because the two caches are independent keys with the same 30s TTL, a fresh permission entry in permCache can be overridden by a stale denial entry for up to 30 seconds. Either invalidate the matching denial entry when permissions are refreshed, check permCache before the denial cache, or use a much shorter TTL for denials.

permissionCacheUsage metric with cache_hit="false" is incremented both when the permission cache entry is absent and when the entry exists but the requested resource is not in the cached scope map. This conflates a true cache miss with a cache hit that results in a permission denial, making the cache hit rate metric misleading. Emit cache_hit="true" when getCachedIdentityPermissions returns a map (the cache entry was found), and only emit "false" on an actual cache miss/error.

issues.descricao: Claims a cached denial blocks access granted within the TTL window; denials are TTL-bounded like the existing permission cache.
Claims trusting cached grants while re-checking cached denials lets stale grants keep access to revoked resources; cached grants were already served for the TTL before this PR.
Claims per-resource denial entries cause unbounded cache memory growth; entries expire after the short TTL.
Claims List now serves stale cached permissions whereas it previously always queried the DB; List was already cache-backed before the change.

Claims the new denial cache is checked before any permission source and never invalidated, so a Check that ran before a resource was created or a grant was added keeps returning Allowed:false for the whole short cache TTL.
Claims the remote authz client still wraps results in a 30s LocalCache, so in remote deployments new dashboards, folders and grants stay invisible for up to 30s.
Claims permissionCacheUsage counts a cache hit that did not grant access as a cache miss.

sugestoes.texto: deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true) cancels the SendGrid scheduled send but never deletes or marks the original rescheduled booking's workflowReminder row, leaving orphaned scheduled reminders in the database. Either delete the row here or mark it cancelled so the cron job can clean it up.

The remindersToCancel query filters only by cancelled: true and scheduledDate, without restricting to method: EMAIL or referenceId: { not: null }. If an SMS or reference-less row is ever flagged cancelled, the SendGrid request will fail because batch_id is missing or wrong. Add method and referenceId filters to match the SendGrid cancellation path.

scheduledReminders.forEach launches all deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder promises concurrently without awaiting or limiting concurrency, creating unbounded fan-out to SendGrid/Twilio when a workflow has many scheduled reminders. Use Promise.all with a concurrency limit (e.g., p-map) or sequential await to avoid overwhelming the downstream APIs.

`remindersToCancel` queries `WorkflowReminder` by the new nullable `cancelled` column and `scheduledDate`, but there is no index on either field. As the table grows this cron query will perform a full table scan. Add a composite index such as `@@index([cancelled, scheduledDate])`.

issues.descricao: The booking-page reschedule path cancels email reminders with immediateDelete=true, which leaves the WorkflowReminder row in the DB, while the dashboard reschedule path marks it cancelled for cleanup, so the two flows are inconsistent.
Claims the code comment overstates the cancel window because the query lacks a lower bound on scheduledDate.
Claims the cron's cancel loop uses an undefined `client` variable, causing a ReferenceError.
Claims the unscheduled-reminders query re-schedules reminders marked cancelled because it lacks a cancelled filter.
Claims a hard-coded "Verification code" placeholder bypasses i18n.
Claims a hard-coded "Verify" button label bypasses i18n.

With immediateDelete=true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancels the SendGrid send but neither deletes nor marks the WorkflowReminder row, leaving orphaned scheduled rows inconsistent with the non-immediate path.
Claims reminders from disabled event types are still sent and can be re-scheduled because they are only marked cancelled.
Notes the isSenderIdNeeded branch removal without reporting a problem.
The new cancelled column is nullable without a default, so existing WorkflowReminder rows get null instead of false.

With immediateDelete=true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without deleting or flagging the WorkflowReminder row, and the callers no longer delete it, so reminder rows are left orphaned in the database.
The reschedule path cancels SendGrid email reminders immediately (immediateDelete=true) instead of flagging them cancelled for the cron, which supposedly accumulates cancelled batches.
When an email reminder is cancelled immediately on reschedule, its WorkflowReminder row is never deleted or marked cancelled, so stale scheduled reminder rows are left in the database.
Claims the cron's cancelled-reminders query can pick rows with a null referenceId and send batch_id:null to SendGrid, aborting cancellation of the remaining reminders.

sugestoes.texto: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result explicitly enables negative-offset slicing and then compares len(results) against a negative offset at line 891, so the extra-row trimming branch is almost never selected and the returned page/cursor is incorrect.

Negative Django slicing (queryset[offset:stop] with offset<0) generates SQL that counts the full result set and skips to the end. An admin can supply a large-magnitude negative offset against the audit-log table, causing an expensive sequential scan and skip without any upper bound on offset magnitude.

issues.descricao: Claims the prev-page trim check uses the raw offset instead of the clamped start_offset, so clamped or negative offsets mis-trim results and return wrong page boundaries.
Claims OptimizedCursorPaginator relies on self.key and self._is_asc that only DateTimePaginator defines, so get_item_key raises AttributeError.
Claims the audit log endpoint imports an OptimizedCursorPaginator class that does not exist.
The prev-cursor trimming check still uses the raw offset instead of start_offset, so when they differ it drops or keeps the wrong row.
Claims OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor drops the +1 adjustment for prev cursors that BasePaginator applies.
Claims OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key omits the callable-key branch from BasePaginator.get_item_key.

sugestoes.texto: The authorization check only matches credential.userId, ignoring team-owned credentials. Team/delegation credentials can have userId null, so legitimate members are denied and the boundary is inconsistent with the existing credentials.delete handler, which accepts teamId and delegates to handleDeleteCredential. Add teamId to the input and verify the caller belongs to the credential's team before deleting cache.

issues.descricao: Claims the cache refresh writes SelectedCalendar.updatedAt while the UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt, so the displayed 'last updated' is never what the refresh sets.
The Delete cached data action is offered for delegation credentials that the component otherwise treats as non-modifiable, because hasCache does not check delegationCredentialId.
The session user query now selects the internal googleChannelId of selected calendars, which could be exposed to the client if the result is returned (e.g. by the me handler).
States that CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx has no data-exposure issue.
States that calendar-cache.repository.ts has no data-exposure issue.
States that selectedCalendar.ts has no data-exposure issue.
States that deleteCache.handler.ts has no data-exposure issue.
States that test-gcal-webhooks.sh has no data-exposure issue.
Claims restricting the credential lookup to `userId: user.id` wrongly rejects team-owned or delegated credentials when deleting the calendar cache.
Claims getCacheStatusByCredentialIds should ignore expired cache rows, otherwise the UI shows a cache timestamp and delete action when no usable cache remains.

sugestoes.texto: If the decoder raises for a message whose message.value is not a BrokerValue, the exception handler cannot complete any offset, so that partition's commits stall forever. The assert isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue) is used as control flow after decoder may already have run. Move the BrokerValue extraction/validation before decoder work and complete the offset on any failure path.

get_committable_offsets iterates range(start, max_offset+1) for every partition while holding the partition lock, so large offset gaps cause unbounded O(max-min) work and block worker threads from completing offsets. Replace the linear scan with a sorted/heap structure that can find the next contiguous completed offset in O(log n).

OrderedQueueWorker.run() emits a metrics.gauge for every single processed message in the finally block, adding per-message overhead on the hot path. Move queue-depth reporting to poll() or sample it instead of recording it for every work item.

Commit loop scans the entire in-flight offset window per partition while holding the partition lock. get_committable_offsets() iterates range(start, max_offset+1) once per second (lines 89-93), so large in-flight windows cause long lock holds and CPU spikes that block submit/complete. Use a sorted structure or track the contiguous completed prefix to find the committable offset in O(log N).

Per-message metrics.gauge adds hot-path overhead. OrderedQueueWorker.run() calls metrics.gauge in the finally block for every processed item (lines 150-156). In a high-throughput consumer this serialization and metrics emission cost per message undercuts the parallelism gains. Move the gauge to poll() or sample it periodically instead of emitting it for every message.

issues.descricao: Claims queue.ShutDown and Queue.shutdown() are unavailable on Python < 3.13, so workers never exit on shutdown.
Claims Python's randomized str hash makes group-to-queue assignment differ across processes, breaking per-subscription ordering and letting two processes handle the same subscription concurrently.
Claims FixedQueuePool.submit leaks an outstanding offset when put() raises after add_offset, permanently blocking commits for the partition.
Claims get_stats/wait_until_empty report empty while items are still in flight because qsize drops when a worker takes an item.
Claims metrics.incr receives len(committable) as the instance argument instead of the amount, so the commit count is always 1.
The offsets_committed metric is incremented by the number of partitions being committed rather than the number of offsets, so its name misdescribes the value.
Claims factory shutdown leaves SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy commit threads running and committing after shutdown.
Claims the committable-offset loop iterates the whole numeric span max_offset - start, burning CPU on large offset gaps every commit cycle.
_get_partition_lock reads and writes partition_locks without a global lock, claimed to let two threads create different locks for one partition and break offset tracking.
States review of queue_consumer.py is incomplete with no issue found.
States review of result_consumer.py is incomplete with no issue found.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Optional.get() is called on RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent(). WHY: When the user has no recovery codes credential, this throws NoSuchElementException and breaks the recovery-code login page. HOW: Guard the .get() with isPresent() or use ifPresent/orElseThrow with a meaningful error/behavior.

WHAT: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the raw generatedCodes list and passes it as the UserCredentialModel challengeResponse to user storage, while local storage uses RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel with hashed codes. WHY: External user storage providers receive unhashed recovery codes, creating a sensitive-data exposure inconsistent with the local hashed storage model. HOW: Pass the hashed RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel data to user storage instead of raw codes, or require/ensure the user storage provider hashes the codes before persistence.

issues.descricao: Claims the recovery-code validator uses non-constant-time String.equals, leaking timing information about stored codes.
Claims raw recovery codes are serialized and persisted in cleartext in user storage instead of hashed.
Claims Optional.get() on RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without isPresent() can throw NoSuchElementException.
Plaintext recovery codes are serialized and sent to user storage providers via updateCredential, while the local path stores only hashed codes.
Recovery codes are sent to user storage providers in plaintext instead of hashed, so a provider may persist working second-factor codes.
The test user storage accepts any of the user's recovery codes rather than the specific requested code number, unlike the local provider.
BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials dereferences getMyUser(user) without a null check, so it throws NullPointerException for a user missing from the provider's map.
Claims recovery code verification compares hashes with String.equals, enabling timing attacks.

sugestoes.texto: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AdminPermissions.onEvent invokes clients().setPermissionsEnabled on every ClientRemovedEvent when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. Because management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled and the two features are independent, deleting a client crashes with UnsupportedOperationException. Make setPermissionsEnabled a no-op or implement V2 cleanup for the client resource.

issues.descricao: Claims the per-client resource lookup uses server.getId() as owner while resources are created with server.getClientId(), so client-specific permissions are never found.
Claims that with both fine-grained features enabled, client deletion calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled and throws UnsupportedOperationException.
Claims the all-clients resource lookup in hasPermission(String) cannot find the resource (owner mismatch or not lazily created), so global client permissions are ignored.
Claims the client management-permissions endpoint returns a 500 under V2 because it calls ClientPermissionsV2 methods that throw UnsupportedOperationException.
Claims hasPermission(client, scope) accepts permissions granted on other resources because it does not filter by resource id, allowing privilege escalation across clients.
Claims getClientsWithPermission runs a separate policy evaluation for every client resource, causing O(N) slowdowns.
ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission runs a full policy evaluation for every client resource of type Clients, so listing clients costs one evaluation per client resource.

On ClientRemovedEvent the AdminPermissions listener calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which throws UnsupportedOperationException in ClientPermissionsV2 when V1 and V2 are both enabled, so client deletion fails.
Claims that with both fine-grained authz V1 and V2 enabled, the ClientRemovedEvent listener calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, which now throws, so client deletion fails.
Claims the test grants CONFIGURE together with MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, so addComposites may succeed because of CONFIGURE and the test would pass even if canMapCompositeRoles were broken.
Claims that under FGAP V2 the client management-permissions GET/PUT endpoints call the throwing ClientPermissionsV2 overrides and return 500.

ClientPermissionsV2 canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles check only fine-grained permissions and not the manage-clients role, claimed to deny role mapping to realm admins unlike V1.
Claims the canView(ClientModel) Javadoc is misleading because V2 never evaluates the per-client VIEW_SCOPE permission.
Claims the tests index getDefaultClientScopes() without size checks and could throw IndexOutOfBoundsException.

sugestoes.texto: Email sending errors are swallowed by a `console.log`, so the user receives a success toast even when notifications failed. Log the error with the app's logger and either surface the failure to the client or ensure partial-failure state is observable.

The organizer lookup passes `booking.userId || 0` to `findFirstOrThrow`, but `userId` can be null (the include already uses `booking.user?.destinationCalendar`). For bookings without an assigned organizer, a team admin/owner or attendee who passes the permission check triggers an unhandled Prisma P2025 error instead of a controlled response. Check for null `userId` and throw a clear `TRPCError` before querying.

issues.descricao: Claims newGuests.includes(attendee.email) misroutes newly added guests whose casing differs from the stored value, but new attendees are stored with exactly the submitted string.
Suggests starting with [] instead of [""] because the empty string may cause validation issues; the empty initial field is intentional and validated.
sendAddGuestsEmails never notifies the newly added guests because the formatted event does not contain them, so the newGuests branch is unreachable.
OrganizerAddGuestsEmail reads calEvent.attendees[0].name without a guard and throws when the attendee list is empty.
The AddGuests dialog error toast shows the raw server error message and code, which could display internal backend details such as Prisma errors to the user.
Swallowing email-sending errors returns success even if notification emails fail; the failure should be surfaced to the UI.
Claims the organizer add-guests email subject uses attendees[0].name, which becomes empty because newly added guests are stored with an empty name.

sugestoes.texto: The English-source path regex `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` does not match locale suffixes that contain digits (e.g. `_es_419.properties`), so for such locales the verifier would compare the translation file against itself instead of the English source and silently pass invalid HTML. Expand the character class to include digits or use a locale-aware parser for the filename.

santizeAnchors only verifies that target anchor tags match English anchor tags in order; it does not check that every English anchor is preserved in the target. A translation can therefore omit links entirely without failing validation. After stripping matched target anchors, also require that no unmatched English anchors remain absent from the target.

The locale regex is missing digits: the pattern used to match locales does not include numeric characters, so locale codes containing digits will not be recognized. Update the regex to include digits in the allowed character class.

The anchor check does not require every English anchor to appear in the target. The validation only verifies anchor tags match the English anchor tag strings, but does not enforce that all English anchors are present in the translated target message. Add a check ensuring every English anchor appears in the target.

issues.descricao: Claims santizeAnchors consumes English matcher groups without validation, so a translation with more anchor tags than the English text gets incorrect results.
Notes that normalizeValue blanks the whole choice expression, so a wrong argument index inside the choice would not be flagged.
Claims the English-file path rewrite is fragile and that a messages file without an English counterpart aborts the build with a RuntimeException.
Notes no test covers allowed tags under POLICY_SOME_HTML, so emptying the allow-list would not fail the suite.
VerifyMessageProperties loads message bundles with PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream), claimed to decode as ISO-8859-1 and produce mojibake and spurious Illegal HTML failures for non-English files.
The message verifier compares English files against themselves, so any anchor tag in an English source, including an unsafe href, is stripped before the HTML sanitizer check and never reported.
Error messages in the verifier include absolute file paths; the comment states no data-exposure defect was found.

sugestoes.texto: Frontend/backend contract mismatch: AnonymousDeviceLimit is declared as int64 so JSON always emits 0 when disabled, but packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts types it as number | undefined. Frontend code checking === undefined to detect an unconfigured limit will incorrectly treat 0 as configured and may enforce a zero-device limit.

issues.descricao: Claims ProvideAnonDBStore's new int64 parameter breaks wire dependency injection because wire.go still registers it.
Claims updateDevice reports ErrDeviceLimitReached for any zero-row update, conflating missing or stale devices with the limit being reached.
Claims anonymous clients can bypass the device limit by omitting the X-Grafana-Device-Id header.
Claims anonymous authentication now fails entirely when TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, instead of the previous non-blocking async tagging.
Claims TagDevice now propagates all tagging errors instead of only the limit error, breaking callers that ignored them.
Claims updateDevice's time window is based on device.UpdatedAt rather than time.Now(), which may not match the intended logic.
ProvideAnonDBStore gained an int64 deviceLimit parameter but is still registered as a wire provider in pkg/server/wire.go, which has no provider for int64, so wire generation or compilation fails.

ProvideAnonDBStore now takes an int64 deviceLimit but is still registered as a Wire provider (with an AnonStore bind) in pkg/server/wire.go; Wire cannot supply an int64, so DI generation and the server build fail.
Claims updateDevice's RowsAffected()==0 check wrongly denies already-registered devices on MySQL because MySQL reports changed rather than matched rows.
CreateOrUpdateDevice runs a full COUNT over the 30-day anon_device table on every anonymous request when a device limit is set.
The 'device limit reached' error string is hard-coded English and bypasses i18n.

sugestoes.texto: Every mutating request spawns an unbounded goroutine with a 10s timeout and no worker pool, backpressure, or panic recovery. Under high write load this creates O(requests) goroutines and can exhaust goroutine/memory resources. Introduce a bounded worker pool or rate-limited queue for the async legacy writes.

issues.descricao: Claims the Equal/NotEqual assertions in the Mode 3 tests can never fail, though the Equal assertion does fail if Delete stops returning the storage result.
Claims the legacy-create goroutine races with the caller on a shared obj that can alias the returned object.
Empty comment.
Every mode-3 write spawns an unbounded goroutine for the legacy store, risking goroutine and memory growth under load.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: fetch_http calls SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without a presence guard. WHY: If the admin sets embeddable_host but leaves embed_by_username blank, any embed request for a missing URL triggers a NoMethodError in the RetrieveTopic job. HOW: Return early if SiteSetting.embed_by_username.blank?, or mirror the guard used in PollFeed#execute.

WHAT: The template closes the if/else block with '<%- end if %>', which is invalid Ruby/ERB syntax. WHY: Rendering embed/best will raise a template syntax error, breaking the embed comments page. HOW: Change line 6 to '<%- end %>'.

WHAT: discourse_expires_in 1.minute runs unconditionally after both the topic-view branch and the render 'loading' branch. WHY: Anonymous requests that hit the loading state will cache that loading page for 60 seconds, so even after the background job imports the topic, repeated requests keep showing 'Loading Discussion...' until the cache expires. HOW: Move the cache header call inside the if topic_id branch, or skip caching when rendering loading.

Claims import_remote passes an unvalidated user-supplied URL to Kernel#open, allowing command execution with '|' or local file reads.
Claims PollFeed fetches SiteSetting.feed_polling_url without validation, letting whoever controls that setting make the server request arbitrary internal or external URLs.
Claims the embed best.html.erb template closes its if block with `end if`, which is invalid Ruby, so every render raises a SyntaxError.
The embed layout interpolates request.referer into an inline JavaScript string with only HTML escaping, so a referer containing a quote can break out of the string and run script.

Claims setting X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL on the embed endpoint disables clickjacking protection and that the referer check can be spoofed.
Claims the cook_method migration default of 1 equals raw_html, so every post would skip cooking and sanitization.
Claims the 'not a url' TopicRetriever spec passes regardless of the InvalidURIError rescue because embeddable_host is blank.
`<%- end if %>` in embed/best.html.erb is not valid Ruby, so the template raises a SyntaxError and the embed page fails to render.
Claims `<%- end if %>` leaves a dangling if modifier that makes the logo output the condition, so the logo renders before the header button.
Claims the embed best action builds the view for current_user and then marks it publicly cacheable, so a staff member's view could be served to anonymous visitors.
fetch_http calls SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without a presence check, raising NoMethodError when the setting is blank.
poll_feed opens the feed URL without a timeout and imports every item without a cap, so a slow or huge feed can tie up a worker.
The TopicRetriever specs mock perform_retrieve, so a bug in invalid_host? would not make them fail.
The EmbedController success tests only assert that mocks are called and would pass even if the controller logic were removed.
poll_feed has no test of feed parsing or TopicEmbed.import; the specs only check the execute guards.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Used backup codes are replaced with `null` in the encrypted array instead of being removed, so an exhausted code list never triggers `MissingBackupCodes`. WHY: After all ten codes are consumed the stored value is `[null, …, null]`, which is truthy; `indexOf` returns -1 and the user is incorrectly told the backup code is wrong rather than that no backup codes remain. HOW: Remove the consumed code with `backupCodes.splice(index, 1)` and add a length check on the decrypted array so `MissingBackupCodes` is thrown when no valid codes remain.

issues.descricao: Claims a caller of the changed TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable still passes two arguments, but that caller uses a different, unchanged API module.
The enable-2FA test asserts toBeTruthy on the un-awaited isChecked() Promise, so it passes regardless of the switch state, including now that the backup-codes step is never dismissed.
Backup codes are compared with indexOf/=== instead of a constant-time comparison, theoretically leaking timing information.
Suggests a clearer post-2FA redirect journey in a file that does not exist.
Claims a 2FA page leaks a polling interval; no such page or interval exists.
Reports no issue.
The first 2FA e2e test asserts toBeTruthy() on an unawaited isChecked() Promise, so it always passes even though the backup-codes step now keeps 2FA unchecked until Close is clicked.
The lost-access/go-back toggle button inside the disable-2FA form lacks type="button", so clicking it is claimed to submit the form and fire handleDisable with empty codes.
Claims the backup-code branch of the 2FA disable route throws on a missing encryption key instead of returning a JSON 500, breaking the client's response.json().

sugestoes.texto: Migration is not reversible: the change method deletes site_settings rows with raw execute, so rake db:rollback raises an IrreversibleMigration. Split into up/down methods or wrap the deletion in a reversible block.

Unprotected parameter access in save_host: params[:embeddable_host][:host] raises NoMethodError when the embeddable_host key is missing, causing a 500 instead of a validation error. Use safe parameter access or require the key before assigning attributes.

The migration uses `def change` with a raw `execute` DELETE statement (line 31); Rails cannot reverse that, so `rake db:rollback` raises ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration. Split the migration into `up`/`down` methods or make the data changes reversible.

save_host reads `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` without checking that the nested `embeddable_host` key is present. A request missing that key raises NoMethodError. Use `params.require(:embeddable_host)` or safe access before assignment.

issues.descricao: Claims expandable_first_post? lost its 'embeddable hosts configured' guard and now expands first posts when no EmbeddableHost exists.
Claims the plural *_ids hydration branch crashes on non-array values and keeps undefined entries for missing ids.
Claims Admin::EmbeddingController#update persists nothing, so the client's saveChanges appears to succeed without saving.
Claims EmbeddingSerializer emits only embeddable_host_ids without sideloading the host records, so the admin host table renders empty.

_hydrateEmbedded now treats every `_ids` key as an embedded collection: it calls `.map` without a null/array check (TypeError on null) and always deletes the original key, replacing real id arrays with undefined lookups when the root has no matching collection.
RestAdapter.basePath replaces only the first underscore of the model type, so an admin model type with several underscores would not match ADMIN_MODELS and would use the wrong base path.
EmbeddableHost.record_for_host returns false on bad input and TopicEmbed.import calls eh.try(:category_id), which is claimed to raise on FalseClass and crash the import for malformed URLs.
Embed host checks now issue a database query via EmbeddableHost.record_for_host on every embed request instead of the previous in-memory site-setting check.
TopicEmbed.import passes a nil category when no embeddable host matches the URL, dropping the old embed_category default.
save_host replaces category_id 0 with the uncategorized category because it uses blank? instead of nil?.
The host input placeholder 'example.com' is hard-coded instead of using I18n.
The EmbeddableHostsController spec only checks inheritance and does not exercise create, update or destroy.
The EmbeddingController spec only checks inheritance and does not exercise show or update.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` without guarding against nil. WHY: `SiteSetting.default_locale` is known to be nil during rake tasks and migrations (see lib/tasks/db.rake:3 `I18n.locale = (SiteSetting.default_locale || :en) rescue :en`), so any translation lookup that reaches this fallback chain raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'to_sym' for nil:NilClass`. HOW: Change line 17 to `[locale, (SiteSetting.default_locale || :en).to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`.

WHAT: FallbackLocaleList#[] recomputes the fallback chain and calls `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` on every translation lookup. WHY: I18n::Backend::Fallbacks invokes `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` on every `I18n.t` call; the previous `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` cached the computed array in a Hash, but this override allocates a new array and re-executes site-setting access per translation, creating hot-path overhead. HOW: Use the Hash storage to memoize, e.g., `super || (self[locale] = [locale, (SiteSetting.default_locale || :en).to_sym, :en].uniq.compact)`, so repeated lookups return the cached array.

WHAT: FallbackLocaleList#[] converts SiteSetting.default_locale to a symbol but leaves the input locale in its original type, so when I18n.locale is a string (set from current_user.effective_locale / SiteSetting.default_locale in application_controller.rb:153-157) the fallback chain contains the same locale as both string and symbol, e.g. ["de", :de, :en]. WHY: Array#uniq does not deduplicate a string and its symbol equivalent, so I18n loads the same locale twice (load_locale tracks @loaded_locales by object identity) and performs redundant fallback lookups. HOW: Normalize locale before composing the chain, e.g. [locale&.to_sym, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact, mirroring the default_locale handling.

issues.descricao: Claims a fallback value cached for a not-yet-loaded locale stays stale after that locale's file is loaded, because ensure_loaded! does not invalidate the translation cache.
Suggests normalizing the locale because a String locale mixed with Symbol fallback entries defeats uniq and causes double lookups or double loading.
Claims a nil default_locale makes FallbackLocaleList#[] raise NoMethodError on every missing translation.
Claims every fallback lookup hits the database or Redis through SiteSetting.default_locale, amplifying per-request load.
Claims a user-controlled locale with regex metacharacters reaches load_locale's Regexp and forces loading of unintended locale files.
Claims @loaded_locales is lazily initialized and shared across threads without synchronization.
I18n.ensure_loaded! reads and initializes @loaded_locales outside LOAD_MUTEX, racing with reload!/load_locale under concurrent requests.
Claims set_locale's `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` (application_controller.rb:159) raises NoMethodError on every request if I18n.fallbacks is not the custom FallbackLocaleList.
FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but leaves it empty, so iterating I18n.fallbacks returns nothing.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: When a calendar reference credential is missing from the user's credentials, handleCancelBooking fetches it via `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` and passes the raw Prisma object to getCalendar. WHY: getCalendar expects a CredentialPayload that includes the resolved app/appName; the raw credential lacks the constructed appName field, so the calendar adapter lookup can fail or select the wrong adapter. HOW: Mirror EventManager’s fallback by including the app relation and mapping the result into a CredentialPayload with appName before calling getCalendar.

issues.descricao: Claims GoogleCalendarService.createEvent/updateEvent dereference an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar when destinationCalendar is null or empty.
destinationCalendar is defaulted to null in some producers and to an empty array in others.
loadUsers no longer selects organization.slug for dynamic-user bookings, so code reading user.organization gets undefined.

Claims that for references without a credentialId, looping over every calendar reference and deleting each against all user calendar credentials produces duplicate or wrong-target delete calls and errors.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The new `delete 'members'` and `put 'members'` routes are bare declarations inside `resources :groups`, so Rails scopes them as member routes with an `:id` segment, but `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` and `#remove_member` read `params.require(:group_id)`. WHY: Every membership add/remove request will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` because the route populates `:id`, not `:group_id`. The JS model also sends `/admin/groups/:id/members.json`. HOW: Change the controller to read `params.require(:id)` (consistent with the route and JS), or declare the routes with a `:group_id` segment so `params[:group_id]` is populated.

WHAT: The new `delete "members"` and `put "members"` routes are declared directly inside `resources :groups`, so Rails treats them as member routes and names the path parameter `:id`, not `:group_id`. WHY: `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` and `#remove_member` call `params.require(:group_id)`, which will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` on every request; the frontend also builds the URL with the group id in the path and does not send a `group_id` param. HOW: Either read `params[:id]` in the controller actions, or change the route declaration to produce `:group_id` (e.g. nested `resources :members` or `resources :groups, param: :group_id`).

issues.descricao: Claims the now-unawaited findMembers() call creates a race where the controller has no member data available when it needs it.
Claims the public group members template iterates a bare members property that resolves to undefined because the controller's model is now the Group object.
Claims add_members/remove_member read params[:group_id] while the route supplies the group id as params[:id], so the actions always fail with ParameterMissing.
Claims add_members does not strip whitespace around comma-separated usernames, so entries like 'alice, bob' silently fail to add members.
Claims the public members endpoint accepts an unbounded or negative limit/offset, letting a caller force loading and serializing the whole membership of a large group.
params[:alias_level].present? is false for 0, so choosing the 'nobody' alias level is ignored.

sugestoes.texto: Making `.contents` a flex container (it is rendered with the `clearfix` class in header.hbs:2) turns the clearfix `:before`/`:after` pseudo-elements defined here into extra flex items because they use `display: table`. This can create unwanted anonymous flex items that affect header alignment/ordering.

issues.descricao: Claims the order mixin's box-ordinal-group values are off by one versus order, so legacy WebKit/Firefox render a different item order.
Making .small-action a flex container is claimed to make the floated buttons ignore float:right, because they would be flex items, so they collapse next to the description.
Claims that removing the 5px bullet margin in .extra-info-wrapper misaligns category bullets because the wrapper's parent is still float-based and order() has no effect.

sugestoes.texto: NewMetricsMiddleware returns a closure that mutates a single captured MetricsMiddleware instance (imw.next). Each invocation of a ClientMiddleware factory must produce an independent wrapper; reusing the same struct means the next pointer and other state are shared across chains. Create a new MetricsMiddleware inside the closure (sharing only the metrics vectors) instead of capturing one instance.

MetricsMiddleware's QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, and CollectMetrics methods dereference req to read PluginContext/Queries/Body without nil checks. LoggerMiddleware guards these same methods with `if req == nil { return m.next... }`. Because MetricsMiddleware is wired before LoggerMiddleware, a nil request panics here instead of passing through safely. Add the same nil-request guards.

For QueryData and CallResource, pluginTarget is called twice per request: once in instrumentPluginRequestSize and again in instrumentPluginRequest. Each call performs a plugin registry lookup. Resolve the target once in the top-level method and pass it down, or merge the size and duration instrumentation to avoid the duplicate lookup.

checkHistogram declares foundLabels outside the loop over metricFamily.Metric and never resets it between iterations. If a metric family contains multiple metrics, the matched-label count from one metric leaks into the next and can cause a false "expected N labels, got M" failure. Reset foundLabels to 0 at the start of each metric iteration.

NewMetricsMiddleware returns a closure that mutates the same captured *MetricsMiddleware instance (imw.next) on every CreateClientMiddleware call. Because client.NewDecorator rebuilds the middleware chain per request, this makes all requests share one metrics wrapper and allows one request's chain construction to overwrite the downstream client while another request is still using it. Return a fresh *MetricsMiddleware from the closure instead of reusing the same pointer.

QueryData and CallResource call pluginTarget twice per request (once in instrumentPluginRequestSize and again in instrumentPluginRequest). This can emit a size metric with one target label and then fail or use a different target for the counter/duration if the registry changes between the two lookups. Compute the target once in the handler and pass it into both instrumentation helpers.

checkHistogram declares foundLabels outside the loop over metricFamily.Metric and never resets it between iterations, so partial label matches can accumulate across different metrics and either match a label set spread across multiple series or error out on an otherwise valid series. Reset foundLabels := 0 at the start of each metric iteration.

issues.descricao: Claims ContextualLoggerMiddleware panics on nil requests because it reads req.PluginContext without a nil guard.
Claims the refactor dropped traceID from the 'Plugin Request Completed' log lines.
Claims the metrics middleware factory mutates a shared instance's next field, causing a data race between chains.
Claims the request-size histogram's HELP text says 'returned' though it measures request sizes.
Claims the test never asserts that request size is not instrumented for CheckHealth/CollectMetrics.
Claims checkHistogram carries foundLabels across metrics and returns errors prematurely.
Claims millisecond durations are truncated by integer division before conversion to float.
Claims the request-size test cases use empty payloads and would not detect a broken size calculation.
Claims the duration metric checks only labels and sample counts, not the observed values.
Claims the duration-seconds histogram check omits status and source labels.
Claims LoggerMiddleware depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware running first and would log without plugin identity if reordered.
Claims the metrics middleware now fails the request when the plugin is not in the registry.
The metrics middleware test never asserts that request size is not recorded for CheckHealth and CollectMetrics.
MetricsMiddleware dereferences req (req.Queries, req.Body, req.PluginContext) without a nil-request guard, unlike LoggerMiddleware, so a nil request would panic.
QueryData and CallResource look up the plugin in the registry twice per request.
Claims ContextualLoggerMiddleware is wasted work when backend request logging is disabled because only LoggerMiddleware consumes its context attributes.

sugestoes.texto: After calling process.kill(), the code immediately overwrites self.processes[process_index] with a new process without joining the old one. This leaves the OS zombie until the parent exits and leaks one zombie per restart per shard. Add process.join() after kill() (with a short timeout) before creating the replacement process.

For the threading fallback used in tests, the code only attempts process.kill() for multiprocessing.Process, so an unhealthy thread is never stopped before a new thread is created for the same shards. The old thread continues running with its own SpansBuffer and can flush the same shards concurrently with the new thread. Either disable restart-on-hang for threading.Thread or use a per-thread stop event and join the old thread before replacing it.

issues.descricao: Splitting the buffer per process makes spans.buffer.max-flush-segments a per-process cap, so with P flusher processes up to P times the configured segments are loaded and flushed per cycle.
Claims the CLI default of 1 makes the one-process-per-shard auto mode unreachable.
